image_description: A close-up, low-angle shot of a vertical traffic light suspended against a clear blue sky. The traffic light housing is dark gray/black with three circular lenses stacked vertically: red (top, illuminated), amber/yellow (middle, unlit but visible), and green (bottom, illuminated). Each lens has a textured, faceted surface typical of LED or prismatic lenses. Visors (hoods) extend over each lens. The unit is mounted to a horizontal mast arm via a bracket on the left side. Wires are visible in the background.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific class identity and rule out misclassification as other street furniture.
To verify the 3D structural integrity of the visors and the depth relationship between the lenses and the housing face.
To check for edge bleeding or fusion between the traffic light and the sky/background, especially around the visors.
To detect subtle texture anomalies in the lens facets or housing material that might indicate AI generation artifacts.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the texture of the lenses. Real traffic lights often have specific prismatic patterns. AI generators sometimes smear these into noise or inconsistent patterns. Also, verify that the visors do not 'melt' into the housing or the sky. The simultaneous illumination of Red and Green is unusual for standard operation (usually one at a time), but physically possible in malfunction or specific arrow configurations; do not flag this as an artifact unless structural issues accompany it, but note it as a semantic oddity if relevant.
